key_big: Microbes are too small to see but are everywhere.
key_sub: Some make curd and medicines; some cause disease.
body_html:
How to think about it

Microorganisms are living things too small to see without a microscope: bacteria, fungi, protozoa, algae and viruses (which reproduce only inside living cells). Many are useful: Lactobacillus makes curd, yeast makes dough rise, Penicillium gives penicillin, Rhizobium fixes nitrogen and decomposers recycle dead matter.

Some cause diseases: tuberculosis and typhoid (bacteria), malaria (a protozoan spread by the female Anopheles mosquito), polio and chickenpox (viruses). Antibiotics work against bacteria, not viruses; vaccines prevent many diseases. Salting, sugar, oil, pasteurisation, drying and refrigeration stop microbes from spoiling food.

Example

Which microbe sets curd?

a bacterium in milk

Answer: Lactobacillus

Example

Does an antibiotic cure a cold?

the cold is viral

Answer: no

Common mistakes

  • Thinking all microbes are harmful.
  • Taking antibiotics for viral infections.
  • Saying malaria is caused by a virus.
